links.reason: Purananuru 246 lists the widow's diet (நறுநெய் தீண்டாது, வேளை வெந்தை, பரற்பெய் பள்ளி) as what the queen refuses, and 248 has a widow eat the alli (அல்லிப் படுஉம் புல்). These are two women's different choices, not incompatible claims about one case, so tension is the wrong type; the shared, codified widow's life is a meaningful same_image, and the teaches states it as historical practice.

Kural 618 says 'பொறியின்மை யார்க்கும் பழியன்று' but blames want of effort; Pazhamozhi 236 uses the first half to defend petitioners who get nothing from a giving king, 'தேற்றார் சிறியர் எனல்வேண்டா', and credits gain to 'நோற்றார்க்கு'. The teaches' point that the Kural's absolution is used without its call to effort is accurate.
links.text_issue: Line 2 வீற்று வழி is unclear.

links.reason: 206 bars entrusting goods to the untested on the pretexts of standing or kinship (சிறந்தார் தமரென்று தேற்றார்கை வையார்), 208 bars handing them with contempt to the worthless (நோக்குமின் என்றிகழ்ந்து நொள்வியார் கைவிடுதல்). The pair covers the respectable and the base keeper, with the owner's lapse (தாம்போற்றின், இகழ்ந்து) the fault in both.

251's 'மன்னவன் ஆணைக்கீழ் மற்றையார் மீக்கூற்றம்' with 'மரத்தின்கீழ் ஆகா மரம்' states single authority, and 253's 'தலைமை கருதும் தகையாரை ... நேர்செய் திருத்தல்' as 'ஓரறையுள் பாம்போ(டு) உடனுறையும் ஆறு' gives the danger of equalling the ambitious. The teaches is accurate and specific.

verses.note: The wife (தாரம்) is listed among things to be guarded like gold, which I take as a gender norm.
Bodily conduct toward elders (குரவர்); no purity or birth rule, so no norm.
A rule of bowing in temple and great house; no count word, so no items.
Line 3 ஒளளியன் is a misprint for ஒள்ளியன்.
Heading is வீட்டு நெறி, but the counsel on death addresses anyone, so all.
The four means against an enemy (sweet words, gifts, division, attack) are the king's.
பார்ப்பார் in the proverb means watchers, not a birth group, so no norm.
The ant, weaver bird and crow are similes, not counted items.
Lines 1-2 point to a specific episode of a poet and a giver, but name no one.
Bodily conduct in the great one's house; spitting is not framed as pollution, so no norm.
